text:
maya: Quick heads-up — I'm bringing up a new embed candidate (bridgecrest-v1) for cross-lingual onboarding. Focus: Spanish/English code-switch queries + Romanian small-n samples. Doing baseline -> quantized comparisons.

omar: Nice. Which eval suites are you running?

maya: Running BridgeBench (our internal multilingual recall suite), Tatoeba en-es/ro, and a small PAWS-X subset for paraphrase robustness. Also a synthetic code-switch set we made from user logs.

liz: Are you testing per-channel quantization (pcq) or symmetric int8?

maya: Both. Baseline fp16, then symmetric int8, then pcq int8. Quick results summary so far: recall@1 (en) fp16 0.873 -> int8(sym) 0.865 -> int8(pcq) 0.868. Spanish recall@1 fp16 0.854 -> int8(sym) 0.782 -> int8(pcq) 0.821. Romanian small sample shows fp16 0.792 -> int8(sym) 0.688 -> int8(pcq) 0.704.

devon: Whoa Spanish dropped a lot on symmetric int8. Any idea if that's clustering shift or norm scaling issue?

maya: Early hypothesis: tokenization differences + subword frequency in Spanish cause weight ranges that symmetric quant clips. pcq less bad but not fully recovered.

omar: Can you share the sampling distribution? Maybe Spanish has more rare word tails because of code-switch tokens.

maya: Pasted a short freq table for a few tokens in the code-switch set:

```
token,count
"qué",462
"que",12980
"como",3301
"lol",47
"checkout",12
"tú",210
```

maya: Also ran a quick cosine histogram compare between fp16 and int8(sym) on 2k Spanish queries — mean cosine delta = -0.042, std = 0.018. For en mean delta = -0.009.

liz: That aligns — larger delta for Spanish. Any calibration step for symmetric int8?

maya: We used default global range per-layer. Skipping per-channel scale made drop worse.

omar: Can you run per-channel with linear quant (pcq) but with a small bias-correction/zero-point opt? Might patch the small shift.

maya: Will do. Also throwing evals through our rerank sanity: top-10 MRR changed from 0.64 -> 0.57 (Spanish sym-int8).

devon: Suggest running a tiny fine-tune calibration on a 1k Spanish subset with distillation-like MSE for last linear layer only — cheap and often recovers a lot.

maya: Good call. I'll try last-layer affine recalibration. Quick command I used to generate embeddings:

```bash
redwood-embed --model bridgecrest-v1 --input-file code_switch_spanish.jsonl --out out.npy --batch 64 --quant-mode int8:symmetric
```

maya: After switching to pcq + last-layer recalib (100 steps lr=1e-4 on small set) Spanish recall@1 improved to 0.835 and mean cosine delta down to -0.015. Romanian moved to 0.731.

omar: Nice improvement. What's the inference perf delta for pcq vs sym?

maya: pcq is ~6% slower on CPU decode path, negligible on GPU. Throughput drop from 1200 qps -> 1130 qps on our batcher.

liz: Worth it if quality is restored. Any weird failure modes (e.g., paraphrase swaps)?

maya: PAWS-X checks: fp16 accuracy 0.88, pcq-recalib 0.86, sym-int8 0.79. Errors tended to be swapping near-neighbor paraphrases where the spanish variant used clitic contractions.

ci-bot: CI: bridgecrest-v1 unit tests passed (tokenizer, forward shapes). Coverage: 92%.

maya: Next steps: 1) Run larger Spanish calibration (5k) and measure drift over time. 2) Add per-file quant calibration to our pipeline. 3) Draft a short runbook for Dedicated customers on when to prefer pcq+recalib.

devon: Could we automate checking mean cosine delta per-locale and bail to fallback (fp16/dedicated) when delta > 0.03?

omar: I like that. Make a metric: locale_delta = mean(abs(cos_fp16 - cos_quant)) and tie alert thresholds.

maya: I'll push a PR to redwood-evals with the metric and a small dashboard in console. I'll also attach a sample failing pair for triage.

liz: Thanks — ping when results land, happy to help write the runbook. :thumbsup:

maya: Pinged @omar for review on the PR. Will update thread when calibrations finish.

omar: Reviewing now. If recalib looks stable, we can promote bridgecrest-v1 to canary on Spanish-heavy routes with auto-fallback to fp16.

maya: Sounds good — logging out for today but will post final numbers tomorrow.
